O plus-que-parfait: o passado do passado: The plus-que-parfait: the past of the past
Formar e usar o plus-que-parfait para co: Form and use the plus-que-parfait to tell what had already happened before another past event, and to put the events of a story in order.
PASSO 1: o plus-que-parfait forma-se com: STEP 1: the plus-que-parfait is formed with the IMPARFAIT of «avoir» or «être» + past participle: «j'avais mangé», «tu avais fini», «il était parti», «nous étions arrivés». STEP 2: the choice of auxiliary is the same as in the passé composé: «aller, venir, arriver, partir, entrer, sortir, rester, naître, mourir» and pronominal verbs take «être». STEP 3: with «être», the participle agrees: «elle était partie», «ils étaient arrivés». STEP 4: the plus-que-parfait marks what happened BEFORE another past event: «Quand je suis arrivé, il était déjà parti.» STEP 5: helpful adverbs: «déjà, pas encore, enfin, finalement». STEP 6: negation: «Je n'avais pas mangé.» «Il n'était pas encore arrivé.» STEP 7: pronouns go before the auxiliary: «Je l'avais vu.» «Je ne l'avais jamais vu.» STEP 8: question: «Avais-tu déjà mangé ?» «Est-ce qu'il était déjà parti ?»
em português o pretérito mais-que-perfei: in English the past perfect is «I had eaten». French builds it the same way, with the imparfait of «avoir»: «j'avais mangé». It is the direct equivalent of «I had eaten», and it is used very often.

Ordenar os fatos de uma história: Putting the events of a story in order
PASSO 1: uma história no passado usa trê: STEP 1: a story in the past uses three layers: plus-que-parfait (what had already happened), passé composé (the events) and imparfait (the setting and habits). STEP 2: example: «La veille, j'avais perdu mes clés (plus-que-parfait). Le lendemain, je suis arrivé en retard (passé composé). Il pleuvait (imparfait) et j'étais fatigué.» STEP 3: time references in the past: «la veille» (the day before), «le lendemain» (the next day), «l'année précédente» (the year before), «deux jours avant» (two days earlier), «une semaine plus tard» (a week later). STEP 4: «dès que» and «après que» with the plus-que-parfait: «Dès qu'il avait fini, il partait.» STEP 5: «avant de» + infinitive: «Avant de partir, j'avais fermé la porte.» STEP 6: «après» + past infinitive: «Après avoir mangé, je suis sorti.» «Après être arrivé, il a appelé.» STEP 7: the past infinitive is formed with «avoir» or «être» in the infinitive + participle: «avoir mangé», «être parti». STEP 8: «après avoir» + participle is only possible if the subject is the same for both verbs: «Après avoir mangé, je suis sorti.»
em português dizemos «depois de comer, s: in English we say «after eating, I went out». French says «après avoir mangé, je suis sorti», with the past infinitive. You cannot say «après manger». The subject must be the same in both parts of the sentence.

PASSO 1: para um dia ruim: «Ce jour-là,: STEP 1: for a bad day: «Ce jour-là, tout allait mal.» STEP 2: earlier causes: «Je m'étais couché tard.» «Mon réveil n'avait pas sonné.» STEP 3: consequences: «J'ai raté mon train.» «Je suis arrivé en retard.» STEP 4: reactions: «Mon chef s'est énervé.» «Heureusement, il m'a pardonné.» STEP 5: linking words: «à cause de», «parce que», «du coup» (so, as a result), «résultat» (result).
em português dizemos «eu tinha dormido t: in English we say «I had gone to bed late, so I missed the train». French does the same with «du coup» or «alors»: «je m'étais couché tard, du coup j'ai raté mon train». «Du coup» is very common in speech and marks a consequence.
Une journée difficile / Um dia difícil: Une journée difficile / A hard day
Naquele dia, tudo começou mal. Na vésper: That day, everything started badly. The day before, I had gone to bed very late and my alarm clock hadn't rung. When I woke up, it was already eight o'clock. I got dressed quickly, but I missed the bus. After waiting twenty minutes, I took a taxi. When I got to the office, I found out that my boss had already left for a meeting. Luckily, my colleague had kept notes for me. By evening I was exhausted, but happy: the worst was behind me.
